issues.description: The problem statement requires that main return 0 to indicate successful execution (problem_statement.md line 21), but the provided solution explicitly sets eax to 1 before returning (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 17). This makes the solution inconsistent with the specification and will confuse students about the intended return value (and may cause automated checks that expect 0 to fail).
issues.suggested_fix: Modify the solution so main returns 0 (e.g., replace 'mov eax, 1' with 'mov eax, 0' or remove the incorrect mov and ensure eax is 0 before ret). This brings the solution into agreement with the problem requirement.

issues.description: The template code does not explicitly set the return value for main (template_repository/helloWorld.asm ends with 'ret' without setting eax). The problem statement states that main must return 0; the absence of an explicit 'mov eax, 0' in the template can leave students uncertain whether they must add a return-value instruction in addition to fixing the register typo.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit return-value instruction in the template (e.g., insert 'mov eax, 0' before 'ret') or include a clear comment in the template indicating that main must return 0. This avoids student confusion about whether to change only the register typo or also set the return value.
